name: GoTo Meeting
tagline: Host small private video meetings through a user-owned Jitsi deployment

pricing.notes: Typical Professional monthly organizer price with annual billing.

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: Up to 150 participants; unlimited meeting duration and cloud recording

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Up to 250 participants; unlimited meeting duration and cloud recording

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Up to 250 participants; custom deployment and support
tiers.notes: Contact sales; price is per organizer

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 organizer, 3 participants per meeting and 40 minutes per meeting
pricing.hiddenCosts: Licenses are for organizers, not attendees; each simultaneous hosted meeting needs a separate organizer license. Enhanced Audio is a separately sold add-on.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For GoTo Meeting, host small private video meetings through a user-owned Jitsi deployment. The hard boundary is media infrastructure, dial-in, recording, admin, integrations, and support, plus real-time media infrastructure and reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Host small private video meetings through a user-owned Jitsi deployment, issue signed room links, and keep recordings only when every participant is clearly informed.
whatYouLose: media infrastructure, dial-in, recording, admin, integrations, and support
ongoingBurden: TURN capacity, codecs, browsers, packet loss, scaling, recording, consent, abuse, monitoring, and incident response
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for GoTo Meeting because video products survive because real-time media quality and global reliability are infrastructure businesses, not weekend interface projects. The recurring cost buys TURN capacity, codecs, browsers, packet loss, scaling, recording, consent, abuse, monitoring, and incident response, not just the visible interface.

alternatives.name: Jitsi Meet
alternatives.desc: Click a room link and meet; enterprise polish and uptime are somebody else’s invoice.

alternatives.name: MiroTalk SFU
alternatives.desc: A capable WebRTC room in one Docker stack, with lobby, whiteboard and recording.

facts.install: Use the public browser demo, or deploy the Ubuntu/Docker Compose stack with a domain, TLS, and exposed WebRTC ports
facts.dataFormat: Live media is forwarded through the selected SFU and is not stored by default; optional recordings are WebM files in the configured recording directory or an S3-compatible bucket.
facts.gapVsPaid: MiroTalk SFU includes rooms, lobby, whiteboard, and recording, but it lacks GoTo Meeting's service-level assurances, native-client maturity, telephony, and managed network operations.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires a public Ubuntu server, DNS/TLS, Docker or Node.js, a wide TCP/UDP media-port range, and usually TURN; free AGPL use also does not include unrestricted rebranding.

alternatives.name: Nextcloud Talk
alternatives.desc: Calls and chat inside Nextcloud; scaling it turns into a TURN-server hobby.

facts.install: Enable the Talk app from the app store inside an existing Nextcloud server; add TURN and the High Performance Backend for harder networks or larger calls
facts.engines: Optional Nextcloud Assistant backends provide transcription, translation, and summaries; ordinary chat and calls do not require an AI model.
facts.dataFormat: Messages and call metadata live in the Nextcloud database, shared files live in the Nextcloud data store, and recordings/transcripts remain on the administrator's configured Nextcloud infrastructure.
facts.gapVsPaid: Nextcloud Talk adds calls and chat to a self-owned suite, but it first requires Nextcloud and then TURN and often the High Performance Backend for the reliability GoTo Meeting manages.
facts.setupBlocker: The apparent one-click install assumes a working Nextcloud server; reliable external calls then require TURN, while larger calls and webinars add the High Performance Backend and substantial networking work.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Professional plan and a small private meeting service DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for GoTo Meeting in an empty repository.
Use Docker Compose, Jitsi Meet, a small Next.js 15 control panel, PostgreSQL, and TURN; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: host small private video meetings through a user-owned Jitsi deployment, issue signed room links, and keep recordings only when every participant is clearly informed.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Deploy Jitsi Meet through pinned Docker images and configure a dedicated TURN service.
Build an owner panel for rooms, signed invitations, expiry, lobby mode, and participant limits.
Show connection diagnostics for camera, microphone, browser, bandwidth, and TURN reachability.
Make recording disabled by default and require an on-screen consent state for every participant.
Store room metadata and audit events, but do not store media unless explicitly enabled.
Add health checks, bandwidth dashboards, backup, restore, upgrade, and incident instructions.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a global media edge network.
Deliberately leave out public webinar scale and telephony.
Deliberately leave out regulated recording, enterprise compliance, and guaranteed support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
